features.title: From scattered setup to maintainable Agent Teams.
features.subtitle: CrewBee focuses on the structures that make agent workflows portable and maintainable: Team assets, execution strength, decision context, and context-isolated delegation.

cards.title: Design different Agent Teams for different tasks and projects
cards.desc: Different tasks need different roles, rules, workflows, and completion criteria. Do not stretch one growing prompt across every kind of work.

cards.title: Simple stays fast. Complex gets support.
cards.desc: CrewBee does not turn multi-agent collaboration into a default ritual. Simple tasks stay single-agent and fast; complex tasks add support agents, review, verification, and completion gates.

cards.title: The main Agent owns the decision context
cards.desc: The main Agent keeps user goals, project constraints, support findings, review feedback, verification results, and risks together for final decisions. Support agents can explore, research, and review, but judgment returns to the main Agent.

cards.title: Context-isolated delegation
cards.desc: Support agents work in dedicated contexts and return high-signal findings to the main Agent. Do not dump the search process and low-value material back into the main context.

why.titleBeforeBreak: The problem is not more agents.
paragraphs: Prompts get copied into different places. Roles become longer flat lists. Rules drift across projects. Review and completion criteria are hard to maintain.
Each project slowly grows an implicit workflow. CrewBee turns those hidden workflows into explicit, structured, runnable Agent Teams.
why.emphasis: The value is not more agents. The value is maintainable Team assets.

how.title: How CrewBee works
how.subtitle: Define Teams as assets, project them into your host, pick a Leader or Executor, and run the workflow that matches the task.

steps.desc: Define the Team mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, tool boundaries, review path, and completion criteria.
CrewBee projects Team definitions into the target Agent Harness as selectable, runnable agents. The current first supported host is OpenCode.
Pick Leader when the task needs ownership, support agents, review, and final closure. Pick Executor when the task is clear enough for direct single-agent execution.
Leader and Executor use different execution paths.

modes.label: Leader
modes.desc: Delegates to support agents, gathers findings, and closes with review-backed completion.

modes.label: Executor
modes.desc: Runs directly as a single-agent path without delegation.

team.title: Teams are engineering assets. Copy, modify, and contribute them.
paragraphs: A CrewBee Team is not a prompt file. It is a structured Team package with a mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, review criteria, and human-readable documentation.
Start with the built-in Coding Team. Copy a template. Adjust roles, shared policy, review flow, and completion criteria. Turn your own agent workflow into a reusable Team.

firstTask.title: Your first CrewBee task
firstTask.subtitle: Open a project in OpenCode, select `coding-leader`, and ask CrewBee to fix a real issue with independent review and completion criteria before closure.

flow: Session start → Read Project Context to restore project positioning, architecture, and current plan
During work → Use summaries to guide code reading and decisions
Session end → Update state, risks, decisions, and next actions
Next session → Continue from the latest context

builders.title: Who should try CrewBee?
builders.subtitle: For people already maintaining prompts, agents, rules, and workflows by hand.

cards.desc: You use coding agents or agent harnesses, but prompts, agents, and rules are getting scattered and hard to maintain.
You use OpenCode today and want a structured Team layer with Leaders, members, review, and delegation.
You maintain prompts, roles, or subagents by hand and feel the pressure of copying, migration, review, and versioning.
You want simple coding tasks to stay lightweight and complex tasks to include exploration, independent review, and completion criteria.

opencode.title: OpenCode-ready today
opencode.description: OpenCode is the current adapter: CrewBee projects Team definitions into selectable agents, binds sessions, and supports structured delegation through the plugin runtime.

inspired.title: Inspired by the open-source Agent ecosystem.
paragraphs: CrewBee is inspired by community projects such as OpenCode and oh-my-openagent. These projects make the value of Agent Team workflows in real development environments clearer.
CrewBee continues in this direction by organizing Agent Teams into manageable, projectable, configurable, and reusable engineering assets.

items.a: No. CrewBee uses prompts, but its core is Team definitions, Agent profiles, Runtime Projection, session binding, and delegation tooling. It turns agent workflows into maintainable, runnable Team assets.

items.q: Is CrewBee a flat agent list?
items.a: No. CrewBee is not just more roles. It emphasizes Teams, Leaders, members, shared policy, workflow, review flow, and completion criteria.

No. CrewBee is designed as a Team definition and projection layer for agent harnesses. OpenCode is the first supported host because it provides a practical plugin path today. The long-term direction is to keep Team definitions portable and adapt them to more agent harnesses over time.

items.q: Does CrewBee make every task multi-agent?
items.a: No. CrewBee is about choosing the right execution strength. Simple tasks can stay fast with a single agent; complex tasks can bring in support agents, review, verification, and completion gates.

items.q: Why does the main agent / Leader matter?
items.a: In complex work, support agents only see part of the picture. CrewBee keeps goals, constraints, support findings, review feedback, verification results, and risks together in the main agent’s decision context.

Support agents do code exploration, research, review, or multimodal reading in dedicated contexts, then return high-signal findings to the main agent. This reduces main-agent context pollution and attention load.

items.q: Where does CrewBee sit in the OpenCode ecosystem?
items.a: CrewBee uses OpenCode as the current adapter, not as its whole identity. It is a Team definition and projection layer that organizes prompts, agents, rules, review flows, and completion criteria into maintainable Team assets that can later be adapted to more agent harnesses.

items.q: Is Project Context fully implemented today?
items.a: Project Context is a roadmap direction, not a fully mature current capability. The goal is to maintain high-signal project summaries across sessions and reduce repeated explanation and repeated code reading.
Today, CrewBee supports OpenCode first. More host adapters are roadmap work.

Yes. CrewBee’s core is Team definition and projection, so you can create ResearchOpsTeam, DocumentationTeam, MarketingOpsTeam, ReleaseOpsTeam, and more. The flagship public example today is the built-in Coding Team.
The easiest contribution is not changing the core runtime. Contribute Team templates, docs, use cases, installation feedback, FAQ improvements, or show your Team in Discussions.
